intro: Five themes moving drug development this week — a quiet clinical cycle, so the heat is in financing and the platform map. Refreshed every Monday.

narratives.headline: Oral GLP-1 is the most crowded frontier in metabolic — and it just took on another entrant
narratives.detail: Corxel reported 'competitive' Phase 2 oral GLP-1 data and lined up a global pivotal, slotting into a field that already runs Novo's oral Wegovy, AstraZeneca's elecoglipron, Pfizer's berobenatide and Structure Therapeutics. No efficacy number is out yet, so this is an entrant signal rather than a validated read — but the direction is unmistakable, and Evaluate's ~$2T-by-2032 forecast names obesity as the single biggest growth driver behind it. When a frontier this dense keeps adding names, the scarce asset is differentiation, not another molecule.

narratives.headline: The IPO window is reopening — but only for proven late-stage stories
narratives.detail: Kardigan's $400M raise and BIO bankers reading an opening 2026 IPO window point the same way, with the explicit caveat that the door is open only to de-risked late-stage assets and track-record teams. In the same cycle Sangamo filed for bankruptcy after a three-decade run with no approved therapy — the early-stage casualty that sharpens the contrast (its assets are still wanted, with Lilly and Astellas bidding, so it reads as a sponsor exit, not a science verdict). The thaw is real but selective: capital is flowing to proven late-stage and starving the unproven, and the gap between the two is widening.

narratives.headline: China-origin assets keep arriving through US NewCos — now reaching the gene-editing frontier
narratives.detail: Serapha Bio launched with $230M around SERP-01, an in-vivo base-editing program for AATD in-licensed from China's YolTech — the same in-license-into-a-US-NewCo structure as Pfizer/Innovent, now extended from antibodies into editing. Innovent's mazdutide turning up across both a MASH read and a new colorectal trial-start in the same window underscores how far that supply now reaches. Evaluate names China's rising pipeline as one of two primary growth drivers to 2032; in the deal feed, China-origin sourcing has become the most durable structural pattern of the run.

narratives.headline: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency is becoming a multi-modality proving ground
narratives.detail: SERP-01 puts in-vivo base editing into AATD, a target already contested by RNAi (Wave, Arrowhead), AAV gene therapy (Krystal) and AI-enabled early detection. The modality story underneath is the shift from ex-vivo editing (Beam, Verve) toward in-vivo, liver-directed work — earlier and riskier, but where the platform has to go to matter at scale. Worth watching as the indication where these approaches finally get measured against each other.

narratives.headline: Cardiovascular is quietly turning back into a place capital wants to build
narratives.detail: Two cardio financing datapoints landed in one cycle — Merck KGaA's Versant-backed cardio NewCo and Kardigan's $400M cardiac IPO — with Osanni's $190M ophthalmology-plus-cardiology round adding a third nearby. After years of cardiology running deal-cold while obesity absorbed the cardiometabolic dollars, this looks like the early edge of a rotation back toward the heart itself. Two cycles isn't a trend, but it's enough to put on the watch list.
